text:
maria: Heads up — after the EU GPU pool migration (00:50–01:10 UTC) apiserver watch_queue_depth on eu cluster spiked and controller-manager reconcile latencies jumped. Seeing 503s on provisioning paths. Anyone looking?

kai: On it. Which metrics are flaring?

maria: watch_queue_depth ~9k on apiserver-eu, apiserver_request_latencies 95p -> ~1.2s, etcd follower lag spikes ~400–600ms, controller-manager queue growth visible. Logs show repeated watch reconnects from gpu-provisioner pods.

oliver: Could be bursty attach/detach churn from the new placement policy. Did we change controller resync or lease durations in that rollout?

tessa: We rolled out the "packed placement" policy at ~00:50 UTC to improve utilization — that causes more attach activity when nodes drain.

maria: Short-term mitigation idea: pause further GPU migrations and reduce provisioner fanout. We know that helps but it's a product/cost trade.

kai: Two quick ops knobs: throttle the provisioner replicas and restart controller-manager with conservative QPS/burst. At apiserver layer rate-limits are coarse but helpful. Also we could tune watch cache buckets to absorb hot-key fans.

oliver: Agreed. I'll scale down provisioner and do a controlled restart of controller-manager.

tessa: Running commands now (scaling + restart):

```bash
kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/gpu-provisioner --replicas=1
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy/controller-manager
# (will patch controller-manager env/flags after restart to lower QPS/burst)
```

maria: Provisioner replicas -> 1. watch_queue_depth halved within ~90s. Still seeing an etcd leader change at 01:20 UTC — follower lag spiking intermittently.

kai: Check etcd snapshot/backup jobs and node disk iops — those can exacerbate follower lag.

oliver: Disk IOPS for etcd nodes on eu-west peaked around 01:18 UTC. Looks like a backup + compaction overlapped with migration.

tessa: I disabled the scheduled backup window for eu-west temporarily and alerted the backups team.

maria: @sre-bot status?

sre-bot: Cluster health summary: apiserver=Degraded, etcd=Degraded (follower_lag_high), controller-manager=Degraded (queue_length_high). Active alerts throttled for 10m to reduce noise.

kai: Proposed action plan:
1) Pause GPU migrations pipeline (stop new node moves)
2) Keep provisioner scaled down until watch queue stabilizes
3) Delay backups/compaction for eu-west for 30m window
4) If metrics don't normalize, failover request routing to eu-central (fallback path)
5) Postmortem + cost tradeoff (reserved capacity vs frequent live moves)

oliver: For the fallback path — note that cross-region egress and attach latency will increase costs and potentially user latency. Need exec signoff before cutover.

tessa: PR filed to pause migration pipeline, awaiting approvals. If approved we'll flip it in ~5m.

maria: Thanks team — initial results look promising after scaling down provisioner and pausing backups. Monitoring for 20m. ETA update in this thread. :eyes: 

oliver: One more note for postmortem: if live migrations keep causing high fanout, consider reserving a small warm GPU pool in eu-west (reserved capacity) to reduce live attach churn. That is more expensive but more predictable.

maria: Logged artifacts to s3 for postmortem: s3://redwood-ops/apiserver-eu-migration-6666001234. Will capture graphs and etcd logs.

kai: I'll follow up with a short postmortem template after we stabilize. Good catch, all. :thumbsup:
